body: ## Expected Behavior Resetting a workflow by an explicit `runId` should operate on that run. If the workflow has no `current execution` — e.g. its current run was deleted while older runs still exist — there is no current run to terminate, so reset should create the new run from the base run and make it the current execution. ## Actual Behavior Reset always resolves the current execution first. When the `current_executions` record is missing, reset returns **"workflow not found" regardless of the `runId` provided** — even though the older run named by `runId` still exists. ## Steps to Reproduce the Problem 1. Create a workflow `wf` and start run A and then run B 1. Terminate and delete run B 1. `temporal workflow reset -w wf -r runA` ## Specifications - Version: 1.31.1 - Platform: OS

comments.body:
I traced the reset path: with an explicit runID, 
getWorkflowLeaseImpl → getWorkflowLease(runID) is called 
directly (consistency_checker.go:246), which appears to 
bypass current_executions lookup at this layer.

This suggests the 'workflow not found' error originates 
either in:
1. GetOrCreateChasmExecution → persistence layer 
   (possibly checks current_executions when loading), or
2. A different code path I haven't found yet

Could someone with more context on the cache/persistence 
loading path point me toward where current_executions is 
checked during GetOrCreateChasmExecution? Happy to continue 
investigating with that pointer."

title: ResetWorkflowExecution returns "workflow not found" when targets an older run
